must: Communication models: **interprocess** (socket, MPI, multicast, overlay), **remote invocation** (request-reply, RPC, RMI), **indirect** (group, pub-sub, queues, shared memory).
**MPI** = library specification (not a language). 6 basics: **Init, Finalize, Comm_size, Comm_rank, Send, Recv**.
Blocking vs non-blocking; send modes: **standard, synchronous, buffered, ready** (Send/Ssend/Bsend/Rsend; I- versions non-blocking).
Collectives: **barrier, broadcast, scatter, gather, reduction**. Communicator + **rank**; default **MPI_COMM_WORLD**.
Request-reply failures: **timeouts, duplicate filtering, reply history**; styles **R, RR, RRA**.
**RPC**: client stub **marshals** args → network → server stub/dispatcher. Sync / async / deferred sync / one-way.
**RMI**: proxy, skeleton, dispatcher, remote reference module; methods on objects with remote object references.
**gRPC** = Google, protobuf + HTTP/2. Group comm ordering: **FIFO, causal, total**. Queues: **Put, Get, Poll (non-blocking), Notify**.
formulas: RPC 10 steps: client→stub→OS → network → OS→server stub→server, then the same back
traps: Two blocking synchronous sends facing each other → **deadlock**.
Pub-sub delivers to **all** subscribers; a queue delivers each message to **one** consumer.
likely: List the steps of an RPC.
Explain blocking vs non-blocking MPI with examples.
tricks: MPI's six = **'Start, Stop, How many, Who am I, Send, Receive'**.
